newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Kenyan minister angry at corruption label.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan minister angry at corruption label.

text.p: Kenya's deputy minister of finance criticised a newspaper on Wednesday for describing his country as "the third most corrupt country in the world".
"Where did you get that rating from?" Mathias Keah asked a journalist from the publication Emerging Markets at a seminar on the sidelines of the African Development Bank's annual meeting.
"Before there is a taker, there has to be a giver," Keah said, calling corruption "a cancer that disrupts investment".
The journalist -- who happened to be chairing the seminar -- said the description had come from Transparency International, an organisation lobbying for better government.
He said this organisation agreed that corruption was not just a problem caused by governments, but was also a consequence of companies seeking to win contracts by illegal means.

The Global Coalition for Africa, an informal grouping of African governments, donors, aid workers and companies, said here on Saturday that it would hold a top-level conference on corruption in Africa at a meeting in Maputo in November.
